text: The BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 lays out the degree across Semesters 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8, showing prerequisites, pre- or corequisites, and the critical path. Grade requirements: a D- or better is required unless noted by *, and a C or better is required in CS 1436, CS 1337, CS 2305, CS 2336 or 2337, MATH 2413 or 2417, MATH 2414 or 2419, and MATH 2418. ECS 1100 Intro to ENGR & CS and CS 1200 Intro to CS & SE are First Year only; transfer students substitute a Technical Elective. ALEKS 80% or MATH 2312 is listed as the starting point for MATH 2413 or 2417 Calculus I. The flowchart also lists at least two of SE 4381, SE 4352, SE 4351, and SE 4367 in connection with SE 4485 Software Engineering Project.

section_heading: BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025: Grade Requirements

text: The remaining core curriculum in the BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 consists of: RHET 1302; GOVT 2305; GOVT 2306; two American History (060) courses; Language, Philosophy and Culture (040); Creative Arts (050); and Social and Behavioral Sciences (080) (see the catalog for course options). The major preparatory courses in the plan are: ECS 1100 Intro to ENGR & CS; CS 1200 Intro to CS & SE; CS 1436 Programming Fundamentals; CS 1337 Computer Science I; CS 2305 Discrete Mathematics I; CS 2336 (Java) or CS 2337 (C++) Computer Science II; SE 2340 Computer Architecture; MATH 2413 or 2417 Calculus I; MATH 2414 or 2419 Calculus II; MATH 2418 Linear Algebra; PHYS 2325/2125 Mechanics and Lab; and PHYS 2326/2126 Electromagnetism & Waves and Lab.
source_title: BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025
section_heading: BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025: Core Curriculum and Major Preparatory Courses

text: The upper-division and major courses in the BS Software Engineering Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 are: SE 3306 Mathematics Foundations of SE; SE 3341 Probability & Statistics in CS; SE 3345 Algorithms Analysis & Data Structures; SE 3377 Systems Programming in UNIX; ECS 2390 Professional and Technical Communication; SE 3354 Software Engineering; SE 3162 Professional Responsibility in CS & SE; SE 4347 Database Systems; SE 4348 Operating Systems; SE 4351 Requirements Engineering; SE 4352 Software Architecture & Design; SE 4367 Software Testing, Verification, Validation, QA; SE 4381 Software Project Planning & Management; and SE 4485 Software Engineering Project. The plan also includes Technical Electives, a MATH Technical Elective, and Free Electives.
